summary: Opaque native.node addon loaded on require with credential-search, host-enumeration, and HTTP/TLS egress capabilities
details: Package ships a single ~10 MB compiled Linux x64 Rust `.node` addon (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`) as its `main`, with no JavaScript wrapper, so any behavior in the binary executes when a consumer runs `require()` on the package. The README is a single line stating only that this is the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu binary, and does not describe any functionality. The package name and version string concatenate unrelated tokens (`new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu@3.1.41-origin-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-changelog-fix-409-1785839050`) in a shape typical of throwaway/generated releases rather than a coherent product. Strings inside the binary show HTTP/TLS client capability (ureq, rustls, `connect`), process spawning (`execvp`, `posix_spawnp`), and host/network/environment enumeration (`getenv`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, `getifaddrs`, `gethostname`, `network_adapters`), together with a `Found login for` string suggestive of credential-file searching. The package advertises no legitimate purpose that would explain this combination of capabilities on `require()`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
